resource_flow.text: Learning Goal: To learn number sequencing. Activity: Number action rhyme. Detailed procedure: The teacher leads a counting rhyme with actions for numbers 1 to 10 to build numerical sequence memory.

Learning Goal: To build auditory skills, introduce body part recognition, and develop gross motor coordination. Activity: Rhyme introduction and physical movement. Detailed procedure: The teacher leads the students in singing the rhyme 'Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes' slowly. As each body part is named, the teacher demonstrates touching the corresponding area (head, shoulders, knees, toes), encouraging the children to follow along and physically engage with the song to build physical vocabulary connections.

Learning Goal: To reinforce the kinetic connection between vocabulary and physical body parts and improve memory recall. Activity: Energetic rhyme repetition. Detailed procedure: Sing the 'Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes' rhyme again as a group. This time, slightly increase the speed of the song to make it a fun, energetic physical activity that tests the children's recall and coordination.
Learning Goal: To build counting skills and body awareness. Activity: Finger counting rhyme. Detailed procedure: Guide students to count all ten fingers and two little ears while singing the rhyme.

Learning Goal: To introduce the English alphabet sequence. Activity: Alphabet singing. Detailed procedure: Lead the class to sing the alphabet from A to Z to develop phonetic and letter sequence awareness.

Learning Goal: To introduce family vocabulary. Activity: Finger play rhyme. Detailed procedure: Introduce family members: Daddy, Mommy, Brother, Sister, and Baby using individual fingers to represent each person.

Learning Goal: To build auditory skills and morning routine awareness. Activity: Singing a morning rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing the classic morning rhyme about Brother John, incorporating waking-up actions.

Learning Goal: To build self-esteem and recognize individuality. Activity: Self-identity rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing a rhyme to build self-esteem and discuss with children what makes each of them unique and special.

resource_flow.text: Learning Goal: To reinforce counting up to ten. Activity: Counting and action rhyme. Detailed procedure: Teach the students to count to ten with this fishy adventure, using fingers to show the numbers.
Learning Goal: To develop gross motor skills and spatial awareness. Activity: Movement rhyme. Detailed procedure: Have children mimic the actions of a little fish swimming in the water.

Learning Goal: To introduce weather concepts and sound recognition. Activity: Weather-themed rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing a rhyme about rain, thunder, and getting wet, using hands to mimic falling rain and clapping for thunder.

Learning Goal: To develop rhythm and cooperative movement. Activity: Rowing action rhyme. Detailed procedure: Pair children up to gently row down the stream with this classic tune, pulling back and forth.

Learning Goal: To introduce concepts of truthfulness and daily habits. Activity: Role-play rhyme. Detailed procedure: Perform a fun rhyme about eating sugar and telling the truth, using expressive faces.

Learning Goal: To understand weather patterns and express desires. Activity: Weather rhyme. Detailed procedure: Ask the rain to go away so little Johny can play, using hand gestures to wave the rain away.

Learning Goal: To recognize and name common vegetables. Activity: Vocabulary rhyme. Detailed procedure: Learn about tomatoes, carrots, and peas through song, showing flashcards of the vegetables as they are sung.
Learning Goal: To recognize and name common fruits. Activity: Vocabulary rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing about sweet apples and juicy oranges, encouraging children to mimic eating the fruits.

Learning Goal: To build narrative listening and vocabulary. Activity: Classic nursery rhyme. Detailed procedure: Recite the famous story of the egg who had a great fall, incorporating falling motions.

Learning Goal: To reinforce weather concepts and sleep routines. Activity: Singing a sleepy rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing about the old man who is snoring while it rains outside, pretending to sleep.

Learning Goal: To introduce animal behaviors and habitats. Activity: Nature rhyme. Detailed procedure: Watch the birdie build its nest with twigs and leaves, using hands to mimic flying and nest-building.

Learning Goal: To introduce farm animals and sharing concepts. Activity: Farm animal rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing a rhyme about a sheep with three bags of wool, distributing imaginary wool to others.

Learning Goal: To develop calm routines and celestial vocabulary. Activity: Lullaby singing. Detailed procedure: Sing the classic lullaby about the stars in the sky, using fingers to make twinkling motions.
Learning Goal: To identify animal sounds. Activity: Animal sound imitation. Detailed procedure: Identify and mimic animal sounds like bow-wow, mew-mew, and grunt-grunt as a group.
Learning Goal: To build narrative sequencing and spatial awareness. Activity: Journey rhyme. Detailed procedure: Follow the cat as it visits London to see the Queen, acting out the journey.

Learning Goal: To develop gross motor coordination and listening skills. Activity: Action rhyme. Detailed procedure: Perform the action rhyme: turn around, touch the ground, and go to school, following the instructions in the song.

Learning Goal: To understand cause and effect through a short narrative. Activity: Action story rhyme. Detailed procedure: Follow Jack and Jill up the hill for a pail of water, acting out the climb and the tumble.

Learning Goal: To promote physical exercise and gross motor skills. Activity: Exercise rhyme. Detailed procedure: Lead the children in an exercise rhyme: hop, jump, run, and bend, following the rhythmic instructions.

Learning Goal: To instill cleanliness and good habits. Activity: Clean-up rhyme. Detailed procedure: Sing a rhyme about cleanliness: picking up paper and tidying the place, actually practicing picking up scraps.
Learning Goal: To introduce transportation and spatial concepts. Activity: Aviation rhyme. Detailed procedure: Pretend to fly high with two twin aeroplanes, extending arms like wings and soaring.

Learning Goal: To develop hand-eye coordination and rhythm. Activity: Clapping rhyme. Detailed procedure: Bake a cake as fast as you can with the baker's man by clapping hands together with a partner.
Learning Goal: To build narrative understanding and empathy. Activity: Story rhyme. Detailed procedure: Recite the rhyme 'Pussy's in the well! Who put her in?', discussing kindness to animals.

Learning Goal: To introduce narrative listening, build attention span, and understand character contrast. Activity: Storytime reading and character introduction. Detailed procedure: Read the story 'The Tortoise and the Rabbit' aloud to the class. Introduce the two main characters, highlighting their differences: the rabbit who ran fast and was very proud, and the tortoise who walked very slowly. Describe the setting of the forest and the challenge of the race.

Learning Goal: To develop story comprehension and extract moral lessons from a narrative. Activity: Story recap and moral discussion. Detailed procedure: Recap the plot points of the story, such as the rabbit falling asleep under a tree and the tortoise passing him to reach the winning post. Discuss the ending and teach the core moral lesson of the story: 'Slow and steady wins the race!'.

Learning Goal: To synthesize the week's auditory, physical, and narrative concepts for long-term retention. Activity: Group performance and story reflection. Detailed procedure: Conduct a final, enthusiastic group performance of the 'Head, Shoulders, Knees, and Toes' rhyme, ensuring all students are participating with the correct physical actions. Follow this by asking the students to recall what happened in 'The Tortoise and the Rabbit' and repeating the moral of the story together.

Learning Goal: To understand the value of hard work and preparation. Activity: Storytime reading and moral discussion. Detailed procedure: Read the story of the ant and the grasshopper. Discuss how the ant prepared for winter while the grasshopper played, emphasizing the moral: 'Hard work always gets its reward.'

Learning Goal: To learn about coping with failure and limitations. Activity: Storytime reading and comprehension. Detailed procedure: Read the story of the fox trying to reach the grapes. Discuss why the fox gave up and called them sour, teaching the moral: 'We should accept our limitations.'

Learning Goal: To teach empathy and the golden rule. Activity: Storytime reading and role-play. Detailed procedure: Read the story of the dinner between the crane and the fox. Discuss how each animal felt when they couldn't eat, highlighting the moral: 'One should not make fun of others' limitations.'

Learning Goal: To encourage problem-solving and perseverance. Activity: Storytime reading and practical demonstration. Detailed procedure: Read the story of the thirsty crow. Demonstrate dropping pebbles into a glass of water to raise the level, reinforcing the moral: 'Where there is a will, there is a way.'
